articleTitle: A Passive Battery Management System for Fast Balancing of Four LiFePO4 Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, a Battery Management System (BMS) is designed and implemented to enable fast balancing during charging of four Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) cells connected in series, designated to replace the classical Lead-Acid battery of a vehicle. The BMS detects when the battery pack is charged and it enables passive balancing of charged cells, which are bypassed through high power resistors. The measured parameters (voltages, current, and temperature) and charging/discharging states can be displayed on LCD and transmitted to other Electronic Control Units (ECUs) using Controller Area Networks (CAN).

articleTitle: Low-Power IoT Devices for Measuring Environmental Values
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents how Pycom, Waspmote and Raspberry Pi devices meet low power requirements as part of Internet of Things (IoT). These technologies improve scalability, efficiency and optimize the structure responding to known IoT drawbacks such as low energy, resources and slow information processing. They are part of applications included in Smart City, Smart Home, Smart Grid, mainly telemetry. Libelium technology, including the Waspmote devices, are presented in this paper. Pycom has a variate set of devices: Pysense having five integrated sensors: temperature, humidity, altitude, pressure and light, LoPy, LoPy4 microcontrollers, Pytrack, SiPy, FiPy, GPy, WiPy, expansion boards. Raspberry Pi is known for being a single board-computer which is running its own operating system (OS). It consumes more power, unless running processes are prioritized for lowering the consumption, which requires a vast Linux knowledge. In this article we present an experiment using Pycom and Pysense which will show its capability for collecting data from the environment. Also, this paper describes how the montage works with Adafruit cloud. Pycom devices functioning in low-power wide-area networks use long range (LoRa) antennas which are especially designed for such networks. This type of antenna helps Pycom montages to save energy and for this to take effect, it must be placed in a LPWAN network. LoRa runs well in exposed environments, but connection can be affected by buildings. Having 14dBm output power, LoRa covers 25 km flat areas.

articleTitle: Energy Management for an Islanded Microgrid Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Microgrids that include renewable energy sources are the latest solution for clean energy generation and use. This paper presents the secondary control of a microgrid operating in islanded mode that consists of several renewable energy sources, one energy storage system, and loads. The day-ahead scheduling problem can be solved in different ways. This paper uses the Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for determining the optimal operation of the solar, geothermal and biomass units of the microgrid, the purpose being cost optimization. The scheduling scheme are made available to the user through a graphical interface. The paper compares the different results obtained using the Particle Swarm optimization algorithm and the Harmony Search Optimization Algorithm.

articleTitle: Automatic battery charging system for electric powered drones
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In order to increase the autonomy of the missions performed with the help of the electrically powered drones, two innovative, complex battery loading solutions were designed and built within the framework of the research, using special platforms in the form of mobile PADs. These solutions follow loading procedures implemented on the drones using different methods: direct contact loading between battery terminals and the PAD power supply system and wireless contactless charging using special kits made up of split induction coils in two synchronized groups. The first one who will be the emitter, located on the PAD and the second one, the receiver, mounted on the drone landing gear. The tested solutions will make an autonomous battery charging process by eliminating the need for a human operator, monitoring and controlling the battery charging process and effectively managing the flight assignment.

articleTitle: State of Charge and State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Lithium-Ion batteries are the source of energy for every mobile device and electric vehicle. That is why the user should be aware about the state of charge (SOC) and the state of health (SOH) of the battery. There are several accurate methods presented in the scientific papers but usually these are computationally intensive so running their signal processing algorithms consumes a significant amount of battery power. Our goal is to trade accuracy for energy efficiency by estimating these parameters analyzing the (current) step response of the battery.

articleTitle: Passenger Detection and Counting Inside Vehicles For eCall- a Review on Current Possibilities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this review, the possibilities of autonomous passenger detection and counting are presented and discussed. Since the main focus is to provide supplementary data for a retrofit eCall system, which is to be relayed to emergency responders, cost-effective solutions are in the main focus, including mechanical seat occupancy, belt status detectors and thermopile or passive IR based optical methods. The use of time of flight (TOF) cameras and gas sensors for passenger counting are also discussed.

articleTitle: Solar Emulator for a Photovoltaic Module
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper describes the design and implementation of a solar photovoltaic (PV) emulator for educational purpose. A solar emulator system is a useful tool in order to estimate power losses due to a daylight period while the photovoltaic panel has a fixed position. Usually, the photovoltaic panels have a fixed position and can't capture the maximum from the solar energy. The proposed solar photovoltaic emulator can be used to determine the optimal position of photovoltaic panel related to the Sun, in order to have the maximum power given by solar panel. Some relevant measurements at the end of the paper confirm this scenario.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Cybersecurity Threats in Smart Grid University of Telecommunications and Post, Sofia, Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this article is presented an overview of the existing solutions for smart grids, and an analysis of the majority cases of cybersecurity threats. The purpose of this article is to define the risks of compromising the confidentiality of the transferred and stored data, and the ability to install a new device into the network. The main hazards coming from unauthorized access to the smart grid devices are analyzed and systematized and recommendations are given to improve security. The proposed smart grid design aims at making the system as safe as possible from the viewpoint of information protection and communication using intelligent communication and control devices.

articleTitle: A Weak-Inversion Cmos Analog Multiplier/Divider Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: A structure that has a weak-inversion biased MOS transistor at its core which can be used to build analog multipliers, dividers, squarers or square rooters is presented. It relies on the exponential dependence of the drain current to the gate-to-source voltage of a MOS transistor that is biased in the weak-inversion region. The proposed circuit produces at the output a current proportional to the gate-to-source voltage that has, conversely, a logarithmic dependence on the drain current, which is set to be the input current. Given that linear operations in the log-domain correspond to exponentiations, multiplications or divisions in the antilog-domain, the proposed structure serves as a building block for analog multipliers, dividers and many other non-linear circuits.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Migration Investigations on SAC-Bi-xMn Solder Alloys
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Water drop (WD) test was applied to get more information about the electrochemical migration (ECM) behaviour on various SAC-Bi-xMn alloys using NaCI and Na2S04 solutions. ECM is sort of electrical short failure process, which can resulted in series failure in case of loaded circuits, when humidity appears on/in a conductor-dielectric-conductor structure. The results show that the higher Mn content solder alloys showed relative low Mean Time To Failure (MTTF) values, while in the case of Bi content solder alloys relative higher MTTF values were calculated.

articleTitle: OCR-based Solution for The Integration of Legacy And-Or Non-Electric Counters in Cloud Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) can provide tele-measurement for legacy utility meters (water, natural gas, electricity etc) and can be accepted as a low-cost extension for the capabilities of these counters and for their time of life. On the other side, the “galvanic separation” provided by optical acquisition of displayed counter values offers the confidence of secure reading - for natural gas meters and similar instruments. Our cost-effective solution enables simple snapshots of counters displays (with simple devices like an “ArdtrCarn” - camera for Arduino embedded solutions), local “edge computing” for image packing (in. BMP format) and tele-transmission via the WiFi hot-spot of the intelligent building. At the server-side, National Instruments software sub-systems - NI Vision Development Module and LabView- provide OCR and cloud aggregation of measured values. Our solution is related to a research project for cloud-based smart metering (the LabVIEW sub-system belongs to the communications work-package). Specific to our contribution is the re-balancing of local and centralized processing, involving an assisted learning phase for the OCR.

articleTitle: Pilot Platform for Remote Monitoring of an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Machine-to-machine (M2M) refers to devices that communicate through Internet-of-Things (IoT), which allow an intelligent monitoring and control of many aspects of our daily lives, with applications in vehicular communication, intelligent transportation systems, smart cities, security, environment, agriculture, health, etc. This paper presents the design and development of a pilot platform for monitoring through Internet of an Electric Vehicle (EV). The platform contains an embedded device installed in a vehicle (EVCANMon) and a software application for a web server (EVWebMon). The EVCANMon gathers different data (location, speed, motor temperature and speed, controller temperature, temperature, voltage and current of the battery pack, state-of-charge, fault codes, etc.) from different Electronic Control Units (ECUs) through the vehicle's Controller Area Network (CAN) and send them using the General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) technology of a GSM local operator. The EVWebMon allows storage of monitored parameters in a MySQL database and visualization and interpretation of data using interactive maps and graphs.

articleTitle: Acquisition and Calibration Interface for Gas Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Calibration is the process of obtaining the most accurate sensor data. The MQ gases sensors are produced to measure different types of gas at the same time but the datasheet formula for calibration are poor. To solve this problem, one thing to do is to know what it is the measured substance and to identify formula. The article presents a method of calibrating gas sensors using LabView. The acquisition system consists in a sensors network, which transmit data to an acquisition board and to the computer. The identification of the calibration equation is used to calibrate gas sensors. The methods used to identify the calibration are linear regression and samples compare.

articleTitle: Smart City Emergency Situations Management System Based on Sensors Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The problem of emergency situations management is a very actual and “hot” topic for big cities. A prompt and a robust response action in this situation is needed and smart cities should provide to citizens protection. Therefore, many research programs are made on this field. The main goals for these researches are to create, implement and develop different types of sensor networks, to be able to predict, prevent and react fast and efficiently on dangerous situations. In general, the final results are limited on data acquisition process and database operations, for statistics or monitoring applications. Based on this idea, the studies and research that will be presented in this paper, are focused on implementing, optimize and test various configurations of smart sensors networks, that are able to collect and store data from various sensors, from an extended area like a city, suitable with “IoT Smart city” concept.

articleTitle: Considerations Regarding Computer Aided Design of a Structure to be Manufactured in Occam Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: There are 10 years since the enunciation of a new electronic manufacturing technology that no longer uses soldering alloy, Occam technology. The new technology comes with significant changes in the way the electronic modules are made because two processes - the fabrication of the printed circuit board and the assembly of the electronic module are replaced by a single one. While there are documented several approaches of the domain from the technologist's point of view, there is not known any document about the designer's point of view, except for some hints from the promoter of the new technology. This paper is focused on the problems that the new approach of realizing the electronic module brings to the designer of the interconnection structure. Since we usually are using Altium Designer as computer aided design software, we investigated what changes occur when designing for Occam technology. The primary change is in the PCB Library where all the land patterns should be smaller. It is expected to get a better understanding of the process and to generate new rules for the designers, as well as for electronic components manufacturers.

articleTitle: Performance Estimation of Scalable e-Learning Systems in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Performance estimation of large scale cloud deployments of web servers is an ongoing challenge for researchers and operations engineers all over the globe. In this paper we propose an approach for performance estimation of cloud environment based on performance metrics and scalable coefficient between number of backend nodes and number of load balancers. An example performance estimation using this methodology is provided for a large automated environment in a public cloud.

articleTitle: A Method for Improving an Active Cooling Solution for LEDs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: High power chip-on-board LEDs dissipate, when operating, a very high amount of heat (up to 80% of consumed energy can be converted into dissipated heat). For a very high power COB (chip-on-board) LED (light-emitting diode) light fitting, 90% of the amount of heat produced by the LED during operation is dissipated through the backplate, thus heat sinking solutions are actively researched. However the rest of 10% is not that well understood, due to various convection conditions. Since each Celsius degree is essential for the component's life span, additional ways of removing this heat need to be considered such as using active air jet cooling onto the LED lens.

articleTitle: SPICE Model of a Piezoelectric Transducer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The necessity of new sources of green energy is evident. While the classic sources of renewable energy (solar, wind, tidal, geothermal energy) begin to take over the energy market, it is time to search for new methods to power low energy consuming devices. A suitable solution is the piezoelectric energy harvesting because it can replace batteries in applications where maintenance or changing those batteries can be difficult. There are multiple possibilities of electric circuits for piezoelectric energy harvesting, therefore building those concepts is expensive and it takes a lot of time. The solution is evident: the simulation of those circuits in order to find the optimal one. The goal of this paper is to develop a SPICE model of a piezoelectric transducer that will be used in simulation of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems. We started from the model of MIDE V22BL piezoelectric transducer developed by Linear Technology and we made another three models for our transducers.

articleTitle: PID Algorithm used for DC Motor Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper aims to present the effects of a PID algorithm controller in a closed loop feedback system. Validation of the results is highlighted by calculating the position of a DC motor in a closed-loop system. The importance of this work comes precisely from the need to test and show the responses of such a system as accurately as possible in order to achieve the desired performance in real time. Over the years, due to the growth of the DC motor market, the need to implement control algorithms and test these devices in a more realistic way through mathematically models has been of the utmost importance, showing also the need for research enterprise. Due to these considerations and, of course, to a technological evolution that contemporary industry is subject to, the need to test such systems is imperative, being present and accepted at the highest standards. Early identification of design problems, repeatability of tests, reduction of development costs and shortened validation process are some of the benefits of this testing and control system.

articleTitle: FPGA-Modelling and Simulation of Simple Encoders for Training Purposes in the University of Ruse
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: An approach applying a laboratory board based on Spartan-6 FPGA is provided in the paper. The board was created at the Department of Electronics at the University of Ruse. It is intended for teaching the courses “Pulse and Digital Devices“ and “Digital Circuits”, introducing the students of the specialties “Electronics” and “Computer Systems and Technologies” to the main issues of digital electronics. The logic blocks in FPGAs can be configured to perform complex combinational functions. In most FPGAs, logic blocks also include memory elements, which may be simple flip-flops. In the courses it is envisaged to study different functional units of combinational type: encoders, decoders, multiplexers, demultiplexers, code converters, digital comparators and various arithmetic circuits. One of the topics covered in the courses is the synthesis and analysis of encoders of decimal digits presented in a binary-decimal code. Implementing such encoders using their schematic presentation and testing it on the board is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Antitamper Conductive Mesh Used for Securing Cryptographic Modules
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Physical unique identity patterns, provided by the electronic components and electric circuits, are used in cryptographic applications in many forms. These patterns can act as secret data or cryptographic keys, rather than embodying them in non-volatile memories. This paper proposes a special antitamper conductive mesh that provides a unique identity pattern that can be used as cryptographic key. This key needs no energy for storage and is automatically compromised in case of tampering. In this way, the antitamper conductive mesh has dual role: physical antitamper structure and secret key. The proposed mesh can protect cryptographic modules, communication terminals, security and IoT devices.

articleTitle: Intelligent Command of An Underground Irrigation and Fertilization System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a solution for intelligent control of an underground irrigation and fertilization system. Irrigation and application of chemical fertilizers (nitrogen) through underground installations is a much more effective method for agricultural crops. This method allows for better control over the way which irrigation and fertilization are performed. The solution proposed in this paper is an intelligent command and control system for irrigation and fertilization using the underground facility. On the one hand, we have a set of input parameters related to soil quality: humidity, temperature and pH and a set of output parameters related to the irrigation system control or application (also via the irrigation system) of the fertilizer. An intelligent algorithm will determine the sequence of commands that will improve the input parameters and reach optimal irrigation and fertilization points. Another smart algorithm will determine the value of the optimal points.

articleTitle: Software System for Simulation Research of Reed-Solomon Decoders in Presence of Noise Applied in Digital Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper describes the processes of detecting and correcting errors, and decoding using (7,3) Reed-Solomon code, based on Galois field GF(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), generated by the primitive irreducible polynomial f(x)=x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+1, after introducing errors in two symbols in the codeword. The paper presents the software system for research of Reed-Solomon decoders in presence of noise in digital communication systems. The material is used in the course “Coding in Telecommunication Systems”, included as optional in the curriculum of the specialty “Telecommunication Systems” for the Bachelor degree at the University of Ruse. In order to better absorption of the material taught active learning methods are applied. An individual assignment is given to each student and he/she has to solve the task during the practical exercises and present it at the end of the classes to the lecturer. The results of using the methodology proposed here are given for the past six academic years. They confirm the benefits of the active learning methods.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of The Performance of a Special Solar Spectrum Simulator for Ruthenium-Based Dye Sensitized Solar Cell Testing Using LED Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, we present the construction of a light-emitting diode (LED)-based solar spectrum simulator, oriented mainly for the testing of dye-sensitized solar cells based on ruthenium and ruthenium-based compounds. The simulator is built with inexpensive off-the-shelf components, and offers good integrability, scalability and the compatibility with incandescent light sources such as halogen lamps. To verify the properties of the simulator, we performed spectrum measurements of the device and cross-referenced them with the standard solar spectrum AM 1.5 for the terrestrial case, and with the known absorption spectrum of ruthenium. Also, we performed a full energy test on a silicon and a ruthenium-based solar cell, in natural solar light and under our simulator, and cross-referenced the quality of the obtained current-voltage characteristics.

articleTitle: Automated Testing System for Cable Assemblies Used in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper is presented a versatile cable assemblies testing system designed for applications in automotive industry. The implementation of the proposed equipment is based on the NI USB 6212 data acquisition board that is used together with a proprietary Lab View application which controls the operation of the whole system. The experimental stand contains a set of specialized connectors used for interconnecting the acquisition system with the ends of the tested cables. Using a predefined set of templates, the system can verify accurately and quickly the correctitude of the connections for cable assemblies having until nine wires. The templates used for tests can be configured by the user. Once the equipment is initially configured, the tests can be performed in an automated manner. The obtained results are presented on a user friendly interface contained by the LabView software application. The proposed system can be used for testing both signal and power cable assemblies, including flexible interconnection structures. The design offers the advantage of a very versatile structure that can be adapted to a multitude of cable types that are encountered in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: FFT Radix2 Core Implemented on FPGA with DSP48 Slices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper is focused on an experimental design of Fast Fourier Transform core implemented in an FPGA. It is well known that frequency domain analysis is very important in digital signal processing application field and wouldn't be possible without Fourier Transform calculation. The novelty and the experimental part of this study lie into an array of complex multipliers based of DSP48 slices within FPGA resources. These multipliers are able to run simultaneously in order to reduce the processing time of the N points FFT. The goal is to calculate the Fourier coefficients from a discrete input sequence of samples. Depending on the bits flipping, the study will describe both FFT (DIT) Decimation In Time and FFT (DIF) Decimation In Frequency algorithm.

articleTitle: Investigations Related to Electrically Conductive Adhesives Pastes Usage on SMT Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the investigations of bonds mechanical strain function of duration of curing at different fixed curing times to evaluate the possibilities of bonding process on SMT line by using electrically conductive adhesives pastes (ECAP). The experiments will be performed by keeping test PCBs up to 30 minutes (5/10/15/20/25/30 min) at 130°C. The test PCBs contain 0Ω 1206 chip resistors having conductive paste traces realized by printing on FR4 support. The paper presents the results and their interpretation of the microfractography analysis of the chip resistors bonds and the energy dispersive X-ray microanalysis (EDXMA) after resistors bonds shear tests as function of curing period. The experiments become a first step for defining ECAP for usage on SMT line in order to extend ECAP applications in electronics.

articleTitle: Intelligent monitoring and planning system for herbicidal processes in agricultural crops
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper we present a solution for monitoring and planning of processes in agriculture. We monitor the parameters related to the state of the crop, in our case the presence of weeds in agricultural crops, but also the parameters related to the machines that are used (in our case the herbicidal plants - the pump current consumption). Planning is done by using an intelligent algorithm, a genetic algorithm, to determine the optimal crop productivity / operating ratio. The paper presents the results of some interdisciplinary researches in: monitoring solutions, radio networks, IT solutions for events collection and processing, artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Medical Device for Communication with Neuromotor Disabled Patients
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In some circumstances, with the aid of assistive technologies, patients having neuromotor disabilities can interact with virtual keyboards by triggering virtual switches or moving a cursor on a screen to select desired items. This paper presents an electronic medical device used in eye tracking systems that helps the neuromotor disabled patients to communicate with the clinicians through a device connected to a computer. The proposed device contains a custom designed electronic module used to acquire the electrooculography signals, an Arduino Leonardo microprocessor board for the signal acquisition and processing, and a PC running a software in form of a visual keyboard. Due to their affections, the neuromotor disabled patients can't speak or write, but present cognitive function and manifest their intentions by moving their eyeballs. The application running an Arduino detects the patients' actions by moving the eyeballs in four directions and selects a key from a virtual keyboard by using dwell time selection method. The proposed medical device has been implemented and tested on simulated patients and the performances in terms accuracy of the desired key selection have been presented.

articleTitle: Monitoring Walnut Orchards With LoRa Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: A wireless sensor network (WSN) can act as a distributed measurement instrument that can offer improved information compared with a single manually operated instrument, especially on large areas such as an orchard. To increase production and fruit quality, and for the optimal use of resources, a low-power wide area network (LPWAN) can be successfully implemented to monitor environmental parameters. This paper presents a solution for the precise monitoring of essential parameters for fruit growing in a walnut orchard with LoRa technology. Also, a characterization of the network lifetime and coverage is performed.

articleTitle: AF Relaying in a Massive Mu-Mimo Ofdm System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Due to the market demands, current communication systems evolve rapidly from existing 4G standard to a future 5G, that implies higher capacity and flexibility. In 4G systems the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique are used to enable higher rates for mobile users, while in 5G it is expected to further increase the performances by using a significantly higher number of antennas (massive MIMO) and cooperative relays for solving the problem of coverage and capacity at the cell border. In this work, massive multiuser MIMO OFDM (MV-MIMO) systems, with 10 to 100 antennas are used, without relay nodes, to evaluate the bit error rate (BER) as a function of the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR). Then, the system is further developed, by introducing amplify-and-forward (AF) relays as intermediaries between the transmitter and the receiver to see if the performances are improved.

articleTitle: Resistive Sensors Network Analog Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This article is focused on developing a multiplexing system used to select and measure the transducers with the inner sensing element based on passive components. Those transducers are used on a very large scale in the hydrotechnical constructions automated monitoring procedure and the main category is represented by the three or four wire resistive transducers. The proposed solution aims to replace the old multiplexing systems based on electromagnetic relays which is strongly affected by the dam's inner environment conditions: excessive humidity, corrosion, etc. Due to those conditions, the relays are subject of premature wear and that leads to an irreversible contact oxidation which is very difficult to be kept under control. From the measurements point of view, the contact oxidation occurrence means “dead times” in the measurement series and the analyses of the dam behavior can be faulty. The alternative solution proposed in this article is based on using analogue switches [5]. From the command point of view the proposed analogue switch is compatible with an electromagnetic relay, from measurement point of view even with analogue switch may be obtained a low R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub> resistance around 0.6 Ω and resistance match between channels below 0.07 Ω.

articleTitle: Sensor Monitoring System for Formula Student Car
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The main purpose of this scientific paper is to simulate basic car functionalities in order to provide relevant data for internal display and external communication. Therefore, the need for a test-bench, a display module, a telemetry module and a sensory data acquisition module is self-explanatory. Our major achievements are having built a cost-effective and reliable Sensor Monitoring System consisting of Arduino based shields with CAN interfacing capabilities and supply sources(Buck Converter), and also having designed and built a test-bench consisting of a Temperature Sensor, an Analog XY Joystick and an RPM rendering functional block. Furthermore, in order to provide portability and easier maneuverability 3D cases have been printed, along with the design and creation of a physical board which would serve as a support for the entire assembly.

articleTitle: Study of the Waterproof Shelter Colour Influence on the Atmospheric Temperature and Humidity Measurements for an Internet of Things Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Atmospheric temperature and humidity are parameters of great interest in precision agriculture or air quality assessment in urban agglomerations. The emergent technology of Internet of Things comes with the possibility of obtaining information from the field using low power consumption devices equipped with sensors and communication circuits. A device for measuring atmospheric temperature and humidity was built and housed in an acrylonitrile butadiene styrene material. Due to the solar irradiance, the body of the enclosure gets warm and could alter the measurements by thermal conductivity and radiant energy. The study investigates the influence on the measurements of these parameters by the colour of the shelter since there are tendencies to cover it with different paints for artistic design reasons. Three different colours were taken into consideration, white, grey and black. Experiments have to be performed simultaneously in order to meet the same input conditions for solar radiation and air humidity.

articleTitle: Far Field Versus Near Field Measurement in Automotive Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The electronic products designed for commercial use must satisfy international Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standards. The radiated emissions (RE) measurement is one of the tests that are mandatory in a full qualification stage in order to validate an electronic product for series production. This paper is a practical approach to help the engineers working in the EMC automotive area find the area with problems from their project layout. We present results obtained in a semi-anechoic chamber (standardized far field test) in comparison with a nearfield scanning technique. The magnetic near-field data are measured by using EMSCAN system and acquired data are used for finding the the source of emissions. In far field we use: a measuring receiver and radiated emissions antennas: monopole, biconical, log-periodic and horn, but in this case we do not have information about the source of emissions.

articleTitle: Configurable Online Test Creation in PHP with Auto Evaluation of Students Running on the Server of the Sun Trackers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the creation of a configurable online test in PHP. The test works with auto evaluation, so the student can know immediately the result of the test. There were also made some adjustments to the tool to make it robust, to make it harder to be tricked, to obtain correct results for the test. The test result and the student name are saved in an SQL database and the test cannot be taken twice. The SQL database is on the same server where the sun trackers log their data. The evaluated test can be printed on paper or in PDF format to have a proof for the given responses and the exact date an hour of the test.

articleTitle: Chaos Statistical Independence in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The Cryptography is the way to secure the personal information in the 21st century. Nowadays a big challenge is the approach to the quantum computational power which it will be the end for the actual cryptosystems. In the public key ciphers the modulo operation is the core because the Euclid algorithm will increase the computational power needed by the eavesdropper. It seams that the new direction on the internet architecture, blockchain, can be a valuable direction for the public key cryptography survival. Here, a new idea on generating hashes will be introduced by using chaotic behaviour and statistical independence.

articleTitle: Electrolytic Capacitor Polarity Determination Based on Electrical Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of several approaches for identification whether an electrolytic capacitor was mounted in correct polarity or not. An original method for the testing of electrolytic capacitors polarity determination developed by the authors, based on measurements is presented. The method uses simple charging-discharging techniques based on voltage measurements, is very fast and requires very low-cost electronic components. The method can be further extended for electrolytic capacitor on-assembly testing.

articleTitle: Weather Monitoring for Predicting Thermal Comfort and Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper analyses weather monitoring systems using various platforms and types of equipment, one of them being Klara, an Android application installed on a smartphone, which produces a multi-day forecast that includes temperature and pressure in the atmosphere. Another system used for weather forecasting is through the Meteotest API, which provides climatic and satellite data for specific geographical coordinates, but also air pollution measurements and back-casting. The thermal comfort using ISO 7730 standard and the energy efficiency for improving indoor environmental comfort powered by photovoltaic installation system was calculated. The use of the RayManPro model led to the determination of PET (Physiological Equivalent Temperature) and TSV (thermal sensation) and to the correlation of data.

articleTitle: Planar Core Transformers Analysis for a Power Distribution Network Concept
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The compactness and high power density requirements for supplying designs make DC-to-DC converters to become an important part of the power distribution network. In this context, the power distribution network (PDN) components have to convert energy with an increased efficiency. Depending on the design complexity, the number of energy conversion elements will have an important contribution to the overall efficiency powering system. Due to the fact that PDN contain just one net for each voltage rail analyzing the power path magnetic components may be of interest. As a continuation of a previous work, the present article will investigate planar core transformer virtual models as part of PDN. The present study aims to investigate the energy conversion quality by extending the analysis over the switching elements. Using Ansys software simulation tools the behavior of converter hard switching embodiments will be subject to multi frequency solver steps from 400 KHz to1.0 MHz.

articleTitle: Broadband RF Adaptive Antenna With Automatic SWR Control by Using MEMS-RF Technology and Microcontroller Process
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This article considers the possibility to create an automated antenna according system, for a broad spectrum of radiofrequency, in order to obtain a optimum tuning between the impedance of the final stage of radiofrequency and the broadcast antenna, based on the reduction of the standing wave ratio parameter, (SWR). Although there are a lot of technical solutions for this problem, the proposed solution uses an MEMS-RF type element and a PID regulator. The tuning element or the actuator is a variable condenser built using MEMS technology, which provides a variable tuning for the antenna depending on the output voltage generated by the microcontroller. The voltage generated by the microcontroller is calculated in order to minimize an analogic voltage, the SWR. The automated tuning function will be reached using a software PID, implemented in an 8-bit microcontroller, which will optimize the broadcast and tuning parameters of the antenna in the working bandwidth. The schematic of the hardware, of the tuning software, and PID controller response of the automated control system are presented.

articleTitle: Tracking Device for Solar Panels
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a prototype which can locate the area of highest sun intensity and track it according to its movement. The device used to track the sun uses a light dependent resistor connected to two stepper motors, used to generate movement of the panel on both vertical and horizontal axis. The motors, connected to their drivers, together with the light dependent resistor and a potentiometer, are connected to the Arduino Uno microcontroller. The purpose of the prototype is to improve the solar panels to generate up to 60% more energy by enabling solar tracking and by ensuring the panels maintain a perpendicular angle to the sun rays. The solar tracking functions compare a defined maximum value with the data coming from the light dependent resistor and find the difference between the two values, then chooses the smallest value, which correlates to the highest sun intensity.

articleTitle: Method for Creating Virtual Copies of Real Labs in a 2D Environment, Representing a 3D Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The study presents a method for creating a graphical virtual copy of real labs. The method is developed for the Engine for Virtual Electrical Engineering Equipment (EVEEE)., which has its own limitations for the virtual components - equipment surfaces., which hold potentiometers., indicators and pluggable sockets should be perpendicular to the line of sight. Initially., an appropriate point of view is chosen and a photo of the lab is taken. Next., the position of each equipment is marked, and a 3D model is created for each equipment, based on high quality photos. The 3D model is exported as a 2D PNG image with a shadow included in the alpha-channel. The modelled equipment is scaled down to fit into the markings of the original image in order to keep the actual dimensions ratio between the equipment. The obtained results show that the method ensures all requirements are met: those of the engine and those that ensure the sense for reality of the virtual reality.

articleTitle: Description of Virtual Equipment in the EVEEE Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper is developed the methodology to describe virtual equipment in the database of the Engine for Virtual Electrical Engineering Equipment (EVEEE). Each equipment is defined on two levels: graphical and functional. The graphical level describes how the equipment, its virtual components and inputs/outputs appear to the user. The functional level includes the circuit schematic, the variables and operations required to operate it as well as the manipulation of the components and their relation to the circuit. The equipment visual and functional representation is defined entirely in the database of the environment, in order to provide the required flexibility and ease of creation.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Johnson Counters Applied in the Educational Process
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: A laboratory board, based on Spartan-6 devices, the most cost-optimized FPGAs, is presented in the paper. It is created at the Department of Electronics at the University of Ruse and it will be used in the educational process. It is intended for teaching the courses “Pulse and Digital Devices” and “Digital Circuits” introducing the students to the main issues of digital electronics based on the connection of the functional capabilities of the digital components with their microelectronic base and their applications in constructing pulse and digital devices. The logic blocks in FPGAs can be configured to perform complex combinational functions. In most FPGAs, logic blocks also include memory elements, simple flip-flops. In the courses, it is envisaged to study different functional units of sequential type: counters, registers, pseudo-random numbers generators, Johnson ring counters, etc. One of the most attractive topics covered in the courses is the synthesis and analysis of Johnson counters. Implementing Johnson counters using their schematic presentation and testing it on the laboratory board is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Fine Tuning of a VCVS Band Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The design of active filters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>. g. Sallen-Key filter, voltage-controlled voltage-source (VCVS) topology or multiple feedbacks filter) is well known, but the resulted filter parameters: corner frequency, damping coefficient, gain, etc., depend on 4 or 5 component parametric dispersion. This paper presents a case study: the tuning method of a 4th order Butterworth band pass filter build with two VCVS active filters. This filter is used in the measuring chain of the signal conditioner of the linear inductive position sensor (LIPS).

articleTitle: Cost Effective Remote Control System for Analog Audio Mixers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: At musical events, all the signals are summed using an audio mixer, then the resulting signal is delivered to the main sound system. In small or medium venues, the placement of the audio mixer is often not optimum (in front of the stage). The sound engineer is in the situation in which he must make the required adjustments while being placed in a corner of the hall or right near the stage. The audience is usually placed directly in the front of the stage. The different placement of the sound engineer and the majority of the public leads to differences between the sound heard by the audience and the mixer operator. To fix this problem, the sound engineer must be able to walk around the venue and adjust the mixer from a distance. The digital audio mixers which already offer remote control are costly. The paper presents a system designed to allow the remote control the attenuation of the audio signals entering an analog mixer using an Android application which can run on a phone or tablet. This allows a critical upgrade to analog audio mixers with much lower costs than an upgrade to a digital mixer would involve.

articleTitle: The Performance of Supercapacitors' Main Parameters According to Topology of the Electrical Circuits in Which They are Used
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The knowledge of supercapacitors (EDLCs - Electrochemical Double-Layer Capacitors)is based on understanding the electrochemical phenomena inside them and on the behavior of the chemical materials used to obtain the electrodes and the electrolyte. For a better understanding regarding the operation of the superconductor, the present paper focuses on: A. Influence of charge-discharge current on different supercapacitor's parameters such as equivalent series resistance (ESR), loss power and time for charge or discharge the supercapacitor. B. Analysis of series and parallel connections of three 22 F / 2.5 V supercapacitors, considering the theoretical and experimental capacitance calculation, as well as the influence of stabilization time after the charging effect on the capacitance value. The influence of these parameters on the behavior of the supercapacitor can affect the conduction mechanisms that lead to the formation of the Helmholtz double layer [1].

articleTitle: The Impact of Technological limitations on The Performances of Metamaterial Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this study, two main types of metamaterial transmission lines are implemented with lumped components and the electrical parameters are analyzed. The transmission lines have been proposed by the authors several years ago and they are used in designing improved microwave devices. This paper presents a study regarding how available components for the lumped elements affect the behavior in frequency of the transmission lines and solutions to get as closely as possible to the ideal model. The solution obtained is validated both by simulation and measurement. The study is useful for further applications which use this type of metamaterial transmission lines.

articleTitle: Hardware Difficulties and Improvements for High Pressure Fuel Pump Solenoid Valve Noise Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a method for noise cancelling of the solenoid valves part of the High Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) used for Gasoline Direct Injection (GDI) engine systems. Furthermore, specific electronic control and appropriate hardware solutions are presented in order to offer a stable valve closing time independent on system parameters such as variable battery voltage and engine bay temperature. Specific electronic control solutions are required to ease the pressure control and noise cancelling algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Sixth Order Band-Pass Gm-C Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper is focused on achieving high-frequency CMOS circuits for continuous-time filters used in the range of tens of megahertz, used in wireless systems. The implementation and the performance of a 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>order differential band-pass filter using the Gm-C (transconductance - capacitor) topology are analyzed. The Butterworth type of approximation is evaluated. The performances of the circuits are proved by using two basic methods to build a high-order filter: one by cascading Tow-Thomas biquads sections and the second one by emulating a passive LC ladder filter. The accuracy of Gm-C filters design is demonstrated by simulating all possible test scenarios. As a main contribution, the design of the building blocks was made based on the mathematical model. A comparison between the synthesis methods has been performed.

articleTitle: Test Bench Concept for Clutch Drive of Automatic DCT Gearboxes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper a test bench concept for the evaluation of the dynamic performances, precision and accuracy of auxiliary electric drives in an automatic gearbox is presented. Due to the separate drive and load controlled supply, the drive system is able to work at any operating point in the Q1 and Q2 quadrants, i.e. with positive torque and sense reversing. It can also be adjusted very precisely both in space, angular (linear) position and in time, operating duration, making it useful in studying positioning errors and reaction delays. At the end of this paper some relevant experimental measurements related to these variable parameters are presented.

articleTitle: Design Rule Checking. Current Challenges Approached With HyperLynx DRC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The technology invades out life every day. The constantly increasing comfort, the better quality of life that we have been meeting for the last decade are strongly based on the everyday equipment that we use and rely on. The Internet of Things concept brings on the discussion small parts and even smaller boards than even the parts should populate. The problem of space on the printed circuit boards correlated with higher frequency of the signals moved around the project defines specific high-speed issues represented by the crosstalk, overshoots, undershoots, reflections etc. The electrical signal geometry is suffering transformations and eventually the whole project might fail. Such high-speed issues might be avoided if rules are set before the routing process or accurate verifications are run. This paper is focused on how HyperLynx DRC from Mentor Graphics can point out design problems at the virtual prototype of the printed circuit board. It is superior to the regular design rule checker build in any printed circuit board solution.

articleTitle: A Simple Procedure to Detect Failed Capacitor Within a Parallel Bank of MLCCs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper provides a practical method for detecting the failed one ceramic capacitor within a parallel mount on PCB and gives a simple way to save time when it needs to replace the bad component. For achieving this goal is using piezoelectric effect encountered in such devices and thermal methods of screening.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Migration of SAC305 Solders and Tin Surface Finish in NaCI Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The impact of chloride ion contamination on electrochemical migration (ECM) of SAC305 lead-free solder alloys, and galvanic tin surface finish was studied using water drop tests and by using an in-situ electrical and optical measuring set up as well. Tests were performed with the use of 3.5 wt NaCI solution. The “A” type SAC305 alloy had a rosin&acid/flux paste ratio of 12.5 wt%, however by the “B” type SAC305 alloy it was only 9.3 wt%. According to the mean-time-to-failure (MTTF) data it was shown that “A” and “B” type solder alloys have approximately the same ECM susceptibility, but in the case of tin surface finish failures happened typically after shorter period of time.

articleTitle: Comparison between deploying an IoT system designed to be used online and one designed to be used offline
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a comparative analysis of a growing technology, which is IoT, between two systems that are using this technology, one which can be accessed globally and another system with local access which is gathering data over a period of time and then connects to internet for a limited period of time to transmit and receive informations. We survey the ability to work with Internet of Things (IoT) and ways how we can work offline. The analysis focuses on the distinctive advantages and disadvantages, between online and offline control, by highlighting the specificity of each, that we believe should be addressed in an IoT system solution, and discuss how they are approached by the proposed solutions.

articleTitle: PI Timing Measurements in High Speed Flash Memory Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a case study on how to prevent the power distribution network's performance of a flash memories related to setup and hold times violations. We first review different high-speed factors [1], and point out how data timing can influence power distribution networks (PDNs) at frequencies in the range of megahertz. Experimental results show that even by applying usual PI recommendations could not solve the errors that appear on the supply voltage and in data waveforms, errors that could lead to incorrect values at the output of the NOR flash memory.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of Passive Cooling Techniques for High-Power Component Clusters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: One of the most significant reasons for thermal defects in electronic systems is having high temperature areas on an electronic printed circuit board caused by multiple heat sources placed in a cluster. The current research focuses on characterizing thermally two possibilities of cooling such areas, one by employing individual heat sinks for each component in the cluster and another with having one heat sink to dissipate the temperature from all components at once. It has been shown that using individual heat sinks for each component has a significant impact on the overall temperature of the system, reducing the temperature with approximately 20 °C, in steady-state conditions. Individual heat sinks can be integrated in all electronic systems where high-power component clusters are used.

articleTitle: Servo Control Based on Pupil Detection Eye Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The proposed article presents a proof of concept developed for the evaluation of eye tracking algorithms based on pupil detection, built around a servo-based pan/tilt platform controlled by pupil movement. An image of the eye is captured using a head mounted infrared video camera, and after the pupil center position is detected, its coordinates are mapped to control the pan and tilt of a servo motor-controlled miniature platform. The system allows efficient real-world evaluation of different eye tracking algorithms and it can have a wide range of application scenarios depending on the type of accessory mounted on the platform.

articleTitle: Studies of Large Area LED Structures on Flexible Substrates
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: These days the solid-state lighting (SSL) is no longer just an emerging technology but a certitude in many domestic and industrial domains. Interconnection of LEDs on flexible substrates in order to create large area structures is one of the important directions of interest for different applications as backlights for flexible displays and flexible lighting sources (LED light softboxes) or wearable devices [1]-[3]. The present work shows the results of investigations related to interconnection of mid power LEDs on flexible substrates. The investigations include the technology of LEDs interconnection and the effect of substrate on maximum power level that can be sustained by the array structure. This power level, observed through thermographical measurements, will have a value determined by the maximum allowed temperature of LEDs and of substrate. We will also present photometric measurements results, as the luminous flux.

articleTitle: A Tunable Transconductor with Temperature and Process Immunity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a tunable transconductor that shows immunity to temperature and process variations. This work builds upon a previous transconductor solution in which the transconductance gain is controlled by the ratio between a tuning current and square root of the bias current. A novel method for generating the bias current is proposed so that the influence of either process or temperature variations on the transconductance is considerably reduced. The solution employs a bandgap circuit that generates a reference voltage and also IPTAT and INTAT currents, the description of which is outside the scope of the current work. The resulting bias current has the appropriate behaviour such that the influence of the process and temperature in the transconductance expression is cancelled out. If the tuning current can be obtained as a linear combination of IPTAT and INTAT, the transconductance will result with good immunity to both process and temperature variations.

articleTitle: Sensor Module for Monitoring Atmospheric Pressure, Temperature and Humidity With Autonomous Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: It has become increasingly significant to be able to monitor environmental parameters in order to reach the best decision possible in a given situation. This can prove true especially for agriculture (for example in agriculture, for better water management). Another important concept is that of energy saving, and of using solar energy respectively. Photovoltaic panels convert solar radiation into electricity that can be then stored in batteries (for example, Lead-Acid, NiMH, Li-Ion). Thus they can be used to supply an autonomous module in a difficult to reach location, where it is challenging to use another energy source. The photovoltaic panel will charge a battery during the day while also providing the energy needed to operate the circuit; at nighttime the circuit is powered by the charged battery. Our project is based on these important concepts and contains a module for transmitting data gathered from different sensors powered by a battery and a second module having the role of receiving data and displaying them both on a liquid crystal display, and on a simple computer or laptop. In the following, block diagrams, implementation and testing of the entire system will be presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Transformations Applied to Image Processing on the RGB LED Display
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The paper considers non-linear transformation applied in contrast adjustment of LED display images. It tackles the challenges of active image adjustments and processing, taking into account the non-linearity of the display element - a LED screen with nonlinear feature. It addresses the contrast adjustment problem, which involves a series of recursive nonlinear transformations. Considering a setting interval between 0 and 1 these will lead to a proportional and equally distant narrowing of the possible values interval for the image signal. For the special case investigated in this paper, the linear command applied to a LED display will produce nonlinear effects in the response obtained over the light intensity. This entails either a digital conversion (a map of corrections for the non-linear values, which will be taken into consideration when addressing the image pixels), or a nonlinear signal command.

articleTitle: Study of Alternative Solution for Aerial Photo Grammetry
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The current trend of fully exploit the potential and positive effects of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) led to the emergence of numerous applications in aerial-survey which is based on aerial imagery acquisition. Replacement of electromechanical stabilizer with a procedural solution applicable in data processing stage is a novelty in the field. The proposed solution for topographic applications meets the technical and legislative requirements imposed for UAVs and aerial photogrammetry, being tested in different configurations. The results demonstrate that this combination of equipment, software and procedures can meet its goal without compromising the quality.

articleTitle: Efficient Navigation of a Robot Based on an Improved Contrast of Colours Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a successful and efficient control method of an autonomous robot that navigates efficiently through a maze using an improved contrast of black and white colours algorithm. The proposed algorithm develops the standard wall follower algorithm with a series of adjacent techniques based on a combination of standard left-hand and right-hand navigation rules. The robot has the ability to store the optimal path in its internal memory, after it reaches the designated destination at least once. The respective algorithm is implemented through a code in Arduino IDE. The architectural assembly of both hardware and software components implemented into the robot is based on the concept of artificial neural networks. It has been observed that this new complex algorithm has improved the robot's success rate at an efficient navigation through the respective maze.

articleTitle: QPSK Transmission System for Machine to Machine Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper are presented the results regarding the design and the implementation of an enhanced digital transmission system dedicated especially for applications in the field of machine to machine communications. The improved performances of the system, regarding the transmission speed, spectral efficiency and the resistance to noises, are ensured by the very efficient and reliable implementation based on quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK) modulation technique. For obtaining a bidirectional communication, the architecture of the proposed design relies on a cascaded configuration. For each direction of communication are used pairs of AD 633 multipliers connected in symmetrical structures that forms a set of balanced quadrature modulators and demodulators. The synchronization of the emission and reception modules that compose the system is realized with a custom scheme that use specialized circuits based on phase-locked-loop principle. Compared with other implementations, the proposed transmission system represents a very suitable solution for direct communication and extended data exchange between various devices, including industrial instrumentation and other equipments that can be integrated into larger networks for increased efficiency.

articleTitle: A Study on the Gm Based Current Mode Capacitance Multipliers Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study of a current mode capacitance multiplier architecture that uses transconductance amplifiers. A frequency analysis carried on the structure built with ideal transconductors reveals an equivalent input impedance model given by a series of a capacitor and a resistor. A second analysis, considering non-ideal effects such as input and output capacitances or non-zero output conductance, shows that the initial model has to be completed with three other elements. It is demonstrated that the parallel input conductance determines the low frequency resistive behavior of the structure. The model resulting from this analysis is validated by simulations of two implementations using transconductance amplifiers that have similar transconductance characteristics but non-equal output conductance.

articleTitle: High Power Switch using IGBT and GaN MOSFET A solution proposal
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: It is known that even state of the art insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBT) have many issues regarding switching. Despite the fact that they combine the high current and low voltage drop in saturation from bipolar transistors and the easy gate-drive from MOSFETs, being suitable for high power and high voltage applications, they have longer switching times. This make IGBTs unsuitable for high frequencies as they would have significant switching losses, because of the rise times and fall times of the voltage across them and current through them. The nowadays commercial available GaN (Gallium Nitride) transistors still cannot achieve the high-power domain where IGBTs are currently used. Then an IGBT and a GaN MOSFET will be mounted in parallel and with a special control strategy would be implemented a fast switch for high power loads. There would be presented the simulation results for the proposed solution and also some practical measurement on an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Optical Distance Measurement System Analysis at Different Color Temperatures of the Light Source Used by Sun Trackers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents an MSA (Measurement System Analysis) for a system which measures distances with video cameras. Distance measurements with video cameras are often used in robotic systems. In our system the robotic system is a sun tracker. To test the robustness of the measurement system, the distance was measured at different color temperatures of the light source, to see if the change in color temperature makes an influence on the accuracy of the measurements. Six Sigma methods were used to determine if the error in the measurement is high or low. The Six Sigma methods were implemented by creating plots with the Minitab statistical software.

articleTitle: Emotion Identification Using Writing System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: An analysis of the texts written by an individual can identify the different states of the individual and the character write. The proposed project aims to identify the subject comportment analyzing the pencil movements. The system used for movement identification are a pencil equipped with the vibration and accelerometer and gyroscope sensors. This system is personalized for each subject and using a parent data for the normal comportment can be identify another state as emotion, fatigue, et.al The sensors data are acquired using Arduino board using serial communication protocol based on two wire. The data are saved in Excel using a Lab View interface. MatLab software is used for data analysis.

articleTitle: Relation Between the Best Subject's Set of Tasks and the Classifier With the Best Performances on This Set
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This study continues another BCI research in which we explored the positive significant impact that could be obtained in tasks classification accuracy only by selecting the individual most appropriate set of mental tasks. In this paper, the same EEG database was used; namely, for each investigated subjects we classified both a classical reference set of four mental tasks (count, letter, math and rotate) and the best set of four mental tasks, determined individually, in the former research. Twenty different classification systems were tested, each of them belonging to one of the following families: decision trees, support vector machines, nearest neighbor classifiers, and ensemble classifiers. In this study two goals were intended: (a) to investigate, in what degree, a distinct relationship could be established between each subject's specific (given) set of tasks and the classifier, and (b) to explore if and how the subjects' individual-selected sets of tasks could impact on the performance ranking of the classifiers. The study results indicated that no particular relationship appeared, but two other important outcomes were emphasized: (a) the consistency of the considerable improvement generated in the classification accuracy by changing, appropriately and for each individual apart, only the set of the analyzed mental tasks, and (2) the enhancing effect of linearization achieved in the input space and only for the subject's proper set of tasks.

articleTitle: Secure Transmission System for Personal Data Acquired Through Optical Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient and secured transmission system for personal data acquired through optical character recognition (OCR) that can be considered a viable solution for the patient data processing issue in the actual medical system. The procedure involves capturing the ID document containing the data through scanning or photography. The image is encrypted, sent to a cloud, decrypted and then processed by an OCR software in order to extract the targeted information. It has also an additional feature that allows the medical personnel to communicate with each other or grant access to specific information of a certain patient through a chat server. Advantages of the structure include the significant decrease in the amount of time, needed for submitting the personal data into the system, as well as the possibility for a medical specialist to consult with one of his homologous, to get a second opinion/expertise.

articleTitle: Practical Method for Emergency Intervention in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: Today almost anyone carries at least one mobile phone. Help in case of emergency can be requested by dialing a special number, like 112. A normal emergency call contains the description of the emergency, its localization by communicating the exact address, the caller identification by giving personal information like name, home address etc. The process becomes challenging if the victim panics and cannot clearly communicate verbally or he is unsure about his current location. In the case of robberies, it can be assumed that the attacker would not let the victim perform an emergency call. The paper proposes a practical emergency intervention method to resolve these critical situations for almost everyone. It can help the user communicate its situation and exact location at a touch of a screen and without arousing the suspicion of the aggressors, if it is the case. The complete architecture, procedures and results obtained with the first prototype are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Some Considerations About Overvoltages During and After The Disconnection of a Photovoltaic Park
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 24th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging​ (SIITME)
abstract: The grid integration of a photovoltaic park requires some rules to be fulfilled, rules stipulated in local normative. One of the common constraint is the voltage and reactive power control. In some cases this could lead to dangerous transient phenomena, associated with overvoltages and current circulations. In this paper such a scenario is discussed showing not only the causes and effects, but also some recommendation to avoid possible damages, based on oscillograms recorded by digital protective relays.

articleTitle: Development of a Personal Life Guard for Swimmers
